title: Viewing Text Files
subtitle: cat, less, head, tail, wc — reading and measuring files from the command line
author: KERNAL Team

content.code:
# cat: print entire file to screen (best for small files)
cat README.md
cat file1.txt file2.txt      # concatenate multiple files
cat -n README.md             # show line numbers

# less: paginated viewer (best for large files)
less /var/log/syslog
# Navigation in less:
#   Space / f  = next page
#   b          = previous page
#   g / G      = go to start / end
#   /search    = search forward
#   n / N      = next / prev search match
#   q          = quit

# head: first N lines (default: 10)
head config.yml          # first 10 lines
head -n 20 config.yml    # first 20 lines
head -20 config.yml      # same thing

# tail: last N lines (default: 10)
tail server.log          # last 10 lines
tail -n 50 server.log    # last 50 lines
tail -f server.log       # -f: follow (live updates — great for logs!)
tail -f /var/log/nginx/access.log  # watch live web traffic

wc README.md           # lines  words  bytes  filename
# → 42  318  2048  README.md

wc -l README.md        # line count only: 42
wc -w essay.txt        # word count only: 1284
wc -c binary.dat       # byte count: 4096

# Count lines in multiple files
wc -l *.js
# → 120 index.js
# → 85  utils.js
# → 205 total

# Count all source files' lines
find . -name '*.py' | xargs wc -l | tail -1  # total lines of Python

content.text: tail -f is indispensable for debugging. It follows a log file in real-time, printing new lines as they are written. Use tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log while testing your app to see errors as they happen. Ctrl+C to stop following.

questions.question: A log file is 50,000 lines. You want to see the last 20 lines and then watch for new entries in real-time. Which command?
questions.explanation: tail -n 20 -f server.log shows the last 20 lines and then enters 'follow' mode (-f), printing new lines as they are appended to the file. This is the standard way to monitor live logs. Ctrl+C exits. Less +G goes to the end but doesn't follow by default.

faq.q: What is the difference between cat and less?
faq.a: cat prints the entire file to the terminal at once — fine for small files, but large files will flood the screen. less shows one page at a time and lets you scroll and search. Always use less for files larger than a few screens. less is a pager: its name is a pun on 'more' (the older pager tool).

examples: tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log is the first command developers run when debugging a 500 error on a live server
wc -l *.js gives a quick metrics view of codebase size across JavaScript files
